events.factual_description: Blues Alley's authorized InstantSeats event page presents Formosan Groove on Monday, November 2, 2026 at 19:00 as part of Emerging Artist Mondays, co-presented with the Taiwan Culture Center of Greater Washington, D.C. The authorized page lists a $25 face-value ticket plus a $7 fee. It describes Formosan Groove as a contemporary fusion project led by Washington-based Taiwanese artist Shin-Yi Lee, rooted in classic Taiwanese songs and rebuilt through jazz harmony, global rhythms, electronic textures and traditional Asian instruments. The project emphasizes instrumental reinterpretations featuring erhu, keyboards and rhythm-centered textures, and the Blues Alley presentation explicitly extends the cultural frame to Taiwanese food. Formosan Groove's official performance calendar independently confirms the November 2 Blues Alley date and links directly to the InstantSeats event. An official Taiwan culture-center bulletin also confirms the November 2, 19:00–22:00 Blues Alley appearance under the Emerging Artist Mondays banner.

en.why_it_matters: Formosan Groove takes century-old and classic Taiwanese melodies out of the nostalgia cabinet and puts them into a live rhythm language: keyboards, erhu, jazz harmony, electronics and groove are used to rearrange the songs rather than decorate them. At Blues Alley the cultural exchange is unusually explicit because the Taiwan Culture Center is co-presenting the night and the project carries its music-and-food idea into the room, turning the set into a small DMV encounter with Taiwanese repertoire as living material.
en.trip_verdict: If November 2 is open, this is an easy local night to use well: Blues Alley gives the project a focused room and the co-presentation adds more context than a routine club stop. I would go if it fits naturally rather than move a harder-to-replace performance around for it.

es.why_it_matters: Formosan Groove saca melodías taiwanesas clásicas y centenarias de la vitrina de la nostalgia y las mete en un lenguaje rítmico vivo: teclados, erhu, armonía de jazz, electrónica y groove sirven para rearmar las canciones, no sólo para adornarlas. En Blues Alley el intercambio cultural es especialmente explícito porque el Taiwan Culture Center copresenta la noche y el proyecto lleva al club su idea de música y comida, convirtiendo el set en un pequeño encuentro del DMV con repertorio taiwanés tratado como material vivo.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 2 de noviembre está libre, es una noche local fácil de aprovechar: Blues Alley le da al proyecto una sala concentrada y la copresentación añade más contexto que una fecha rutinaria de club. Iría si embona naturalmente, sin mover otro concierto más difícil de reemplazar.
